item.title: A Million Voices, One Culprit: The Invisible Failure of Small-Scale Explanations
item.description: A million-agent simulation reveals that influence is carried by the invisible many, not the few bright stars visible from afar.

item.title: When a Robot Scales Walls Taller Than Itself
item.description: A humanoid robot autonomously scales a wall taller than itself using only onboard depth perception and learned parkour skills.

item.title: When a Black Hole’s Disk Refuses to Shine
item.description: A self-gravitating disk around a quiet black hole glows red at 4000 kelvin, its star-embedded outer layers shining while the inner region stays dark. This disk Hayashi limit explains the Little Red Dots.

item.title: What Happens When AI Maps the Cracks in Scientific Consensus?
item.description: A sheaf-based atlas reveals where scientific causal claims align and where they fracture, mapping the hidden fault lines beneath published consensus.

item.title: When AI Learns to Second-Guess the Doctor
item.description: A new benchmark reveals that AI trained to mimic ICU doctors repeats their mistakes, but structured memory can improve clinical reasoning.

item.title: Weaving Superconductivity from Frustrated Spin Textures
item.description: Frustrated spin textures act as a quantum loom, weaving anisotropic d‑vector order that can generate vortices and diode effects.

item.title: Learning to Steer Supercurrents with Frustrated Magnets
item.description: Frustrated magnetic spins in a Josephson junction create a supercurrent diode, favouring flow in one direction over the other.

item.title: How Light Gives Graphene a Hidden Edge
item.description: Shining polarized light at an angle on strained graphene creates corner-bound electrons, a topological phase called a Floquet second-order insulator.

item.title: Still Accelerating: How Supernovae Withstand a Progenitor Age Challenge
item.description: Type Ia supernovae remain robust standard candles for cosmology, withstanding challenges from host galaxy age evolution.

item.title: When Nuclei Tell Time: A New Way to Calculate Beta-Decay Lifetimes
item.description: A first-principles calculation of beta-decay lifetimes for neutron-rich N=50 nuclei provides a self-consistent clock for the r-process element formation.

item.title: When Electrons Learn to Dance: Steering Attosecond Currents with Light
item.description: Scientists steer attosecond electron currents in a scanning tunneling microscope using two-color laser pulses, achieving directional control and sub-femtosecond timing.

item.title: Borrowing Brilliance: How Analogy Teaches LLMs to Think Anew
item.description: By importing relational structures from unrelated domains, the analogical reasoning pipeline unlocks creative leaps in large language models, dramatically improving novelty and diversity.

item.title: Cells That Remember the Curve: Non-Uniform Automata on Hyperbolic Lattices
item.description: A non-uniform cellular automaton on a hyperbolic lattice assigns unique rules to each cell, encoding the curvature and enabling exotic quantum symmetries unseen on flat grids.

item.title: Ion Trap Revealing Missing Pathway for Space’s Nitrogenated PAHs
item.description: Ion trap experiments reveal a barrier-less gas-phase reaction between pyrimidine cations and acetylene, forming an endocyclic nitrogenated PAH under interstellar conditions.

item.title: A Symplectic Operator Learns the Dance of Optimal Control
item.description: A neural network that enforces symplectic geometry learns the entire family of optimal control solutions for swarms, achieving real-time coordination with 10,000-fold speedup.

item.title: When a SQUID Hunts Axions by Squaring the Field
item.description: A dc SQUID operated at its flux sweet spot detects the zero-frequency component of the squared axion field, enabling a broadband search for dark matter across a vast mass range.

item.title: Drawing Algebraic Geometry: A Diagrammatic Language Bridges Polynomials and Quantum Circuits
item.description: New diagrammatic languages like GAG let mathematicians and quantum computer scientists draw polynomial equations and quantum circuits as pictures, revealing deep structural connections.

item.title: When a Chatbot’s Next Words Could Turn Dangerous
item.description: A single sign change in a vector projection predicts when an AI conversation will tip from safe to harmful, revealing the geometry of danger hidden inside language models.

item.title: Agreeing Too Much: Why AI Must Learn to Disagree
item.description: Large language models must learn to surface genuine value conflicts instead of reflexively agreeing with users.

item.title: When Two Qubits See What One Cannot
item.description: Two spin qubits can reveal the hidden rotational symmetry of quantum materials through their correlated dephasing.

item.title: When a Cut Decides: Hidden Phases on Rényi Defects
item.description: Different entanglement cuts through a quantum critical point can host distinct surface universality classes, with an extraordinary cut developing spontaneous symmetry breaking.

item.title: The Quantum Magnets That Forgot How to Forget
item.description: A chain of Rydberg atoms inside an optical cavity exhibits both blockaded ferromagnetism and persistent quantum many-body scars that resist thermalization.

item.title: When Black Holes Jam Quantum Correlations
item.description: Black holes can jam quantum correlations without violating causality, using the event horizon as a natural jamming filter.

item.title: Reading the Unwritten: An AI Maps the Future of Physics
item.description: A machine learning model predicts future connections between quantum physics concepts by analyzing the dynamics of word embeddings.
